v1.kill_reason: Crowded subject (JSON/YAML/TOML parsers are in the CROWDED list) with the same deliverable and grading as the public yaml-test-suite event-stream benchmark. Mutations are the only delta and do not clearly differentiate it. Also, the grader's libyaml cross-check is YAML 1.1, which conflicts with a 1.2 oracle. Recommendation: do not pursue as is; a non-YAML-conformance variant would need a separate seed.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of frontier results; difficulty claims are self-asserted.

Build.why: Several days for reference plus grader cross-check; smoke probe is amber with no usable report.

Hor.why: 4 h tier is plausible for a 2-3k line parser but the scope is closer to 2-4 h of focused work.

Lic.why: MIT suite; cross-check parsers are grader-side only.

Multi.why: Clear buckets: block/flow, anchors/tags, multi-doc, error classes.

Nov.why: CROWDED list names JSON/YAML/TOML parsers; same subject and event-stream deliverable as public benchmarks; mutations are the only delta.

Real.why: Public MIT repo at a pinned tag with published event streams.

Ref.why: Reference is ours, unwritten, and its 'scores 1' is unverified; no upstream measured reference.

Seal.why: Hidden remainder is public and widely vendored (libfyaml, yaml-rust2 crates, rapidyaml); sealing depends on image hygiene.

Surf.why: About 351 suite cases plus a generator of mutations; count of 351 not verified.

spike_plan.kill_if: Case count well below 300 or not reproducible; libyaml disagrees with test.event on more than about 10% of non-error cases (a 1.1-vs-1.2 gap the grader cannot resolve); or the baseline already scores near 1 on the visible set.
spike_plan.pass_if: Counted cases approx. 351 and reproducible; libyaml agrees with test.event on at least 95% of non-error cases; the baseline scores strictly between 0 and 1 across buckets; mutation output is deterministic.
steps: In a networked throwaway Linux container, clone yaml/yaml-test-suite at tag v2022-01-17 and at branch/tag data-2022-01-17; count case directories and test.event files to verify the ~351 figure.
Check that every case with test.event has in.yaml, and list the error-marked cases separately.
Install libyaml dev package, write a tiny event-dumper wrapper in C, and run it over all cases; compare its event output to test.event and record agreement per case, split by error and non-error.
Write a 30-minute baseline (block mappings and scalars only) and score it on the same cases to check that the partial-credit curve has buckets.
Run the grader's mutation generator twice with the same seed and confirm identical mutated cases; confirm libyaml-vs-suite disagreements are rare enough to use as a cross-check.

v1.summary: The seed's repository, MIT licence, and tag v2022-01-17 are confirmed, but the ~351-case count is not verified (src listing truncated at 100). The idea is killed as K1 because YAML parsers are a crowded subject with the same deliverable and event-stream grading as the public yaml-test-suite benchmark, and the mutations are the only difference.
